evidence.quote: DM: We begin in the darkness as we catch a glimpse into the mind of Lord Rhodar von Glauer, looking at the sad creatures bumbling in the dark before him in another misguided attempt to take his power, he assumes. Watching them, he thinks back. He can still remember his days among the living. He joined the Eyes of Vedmakov out of a sense of patriotism, he supposes. Misguided, it turned out. In those days the Rodnya Okolov was strong. The eyes and the shield, people said, Okolov and Morozmir, the watchers and the protectors, the heart of the defense of Ursk against the dragons of the North, who are always seeking to reclaim their power, to rise again in another great host, to see another Vimfrost take all the north. He took to the magic of Okolov so easily. Even now the watcher's magic flows through him. Those fool adventurers probably don't realize he's been watching them since they set foot on Drachen's Peak, waiting patiently. They have shown skill and cleverness, though. They'll make good lieutenants. No slow cold death in the snow for them, their minds consumed by Putrid Agnes. The death of servitude in his army is what they deserve and what they'll get.
Delwath: Is the mountain stable?
DM: The mountain is—may be stable, although Putrid Agnes seems to have scarpered from the scene. Whether that's a good or a bad sign is not immediately obvious.
Delwath: I think we hike right?
Riswynn: Down the mountain to the campsite and rest long enough to get teleported the heck out of here.
Seeker: Yeah, if we can sleep, we can teleport.

DM: It's, it's mid afternoon now, and it takes you a good 4 h to trek down to somewhere that's sort of comfortable and safe to rest. So the time you reach a safe campground, the sun is setting. It's maybe 7 PM. And you, you know, establish your camp and get settled, and as you think and recall the dangers of the battle in your successful flight from the collapsing tower, you all level up.

relations.note: The mountain approach and descent identify the setting; no height or exact summit geometry is reconstructed.
